QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_22

question.text: In the context of a Category II PE fund, the 'J-curve' refers to:

answer.text: The trajectory of management fees over fund life
The shape of the fund's asset allocation chart
The steep initial drop in IRR during vintage years followed by recovery and peak returns near maturity
The relationship between hurdle rate and catch-up rate

explanation.text: The Logic: The J-curve describes negative early cash flows and IRRs during the vintage years of a private equity / Category I/II AIF, followed by positive cash flows and rising/peaking IRRs as exits and distributions occur. The Trap: Options A, B and D describe unrelated fund concepts; none of them captures the cash-flow / IRR trajectory that defines the J-curve. Note: The J-curve pattern is documented in the fund performance chapter of the workbook for Category I/II AIFs.
